brief: Calculate two periods of growth when earlier gains remain in the base, and distinguish this toy model from a guaranteed return.

en-US.scenario: Fictional US-dollar examples for "Growth on earlier growth"; illustrative amounts, not current prices or product offers. No assumption of salary, bank ownership or spare income.

es-MX.scenario: Ejemplos ficticios en pesos mexicanos para "Crecimiento sobre crecimiento"; montos ilustrativos, no precios vigentes ni ofertas. No se supone nómina, cuenta bancaria ni dinero sobrante.

pt-BR.scenario: Exemplos fictícios em reais para "Crescimento sobre crescimento"; valores ilustrativos, não preços atuais nem ofertas. Sem supor salário, conta bancária ou dinheiro sobrando.

objective.observable_action: Calculate two periods of growth when earlier gains remain in the base, and distinguish this toy model from a guaranteed return.
objective.success_criterion: Complete the fresh-context transfer using only its visible information.

instruction.relevance: Growth can apply to earlier gains when they stay in the balance. These dollar examples use a fixed invented rate.
instruction.misconception: Applying every period percentage only to the original amount or assuming a constant-rate illustration promises an actual investment result.
instruction.numeracy_support: Repeat the previously taught percentage calculation using the updated base; no exponent formula is assumed.

evidence.reasoning: At a fictional 10% per period, 100 becomes 110. Keeping the gain makes 110 the next base.
Next, 10% of 110 is 11, giving 121. Growth only on the original 100 would add another 10 instead.
Toy model: 100 dollars, no fees or withdrawals. At 10% over two years, predict and compare simple versus compound growth.
The gain is added to the starting amount.
Retained growth becomes part of the next period base.
The growth amount is a share of this starting balance.
Growth is calculated on the updated base, including retained gains.
The chart shows a model, not a guaranteed investment result.
The second period uses the updated amount including the first gain.
